name: Shihhi Arabic
notes:
REGISTRY STUB (not a modelled G2P target). Placed so the ancestry graph covers every living ISO 639-3 language. No orthography or phonology is claimed: script is Zyyy (undetermined) until a cited description is encoded. Classification and coordinates follow Glottolog.

RESOLVES TO ITS PARENT'S TABLE, WHICH IS A PLACEHOLDER. This spec declared a parent and no `graphemes_base`, so it produced no phonology at all and the code resolved to an empty table. It now inherits, so the code reaches a usable table. That table is the parent's and is NOT a claim about this variety. Graphemes inherited from ar-OM because Ruʾūs al-Jibāl is in Musandam, Oman.

A DESCRIPTION EXISTS AND IS NOT YET READ IN. Bernabela (2011), a Leiden MA thesis, describes Shiḥḥi: the Old Arabic interdentals ṯ, ḏ and ḏ̣ have plosive reflexes t, d and ḍ (§1.1.10 p.26), and Old Arabic ʕ is largely lost with a glottal stop as its primary reflex (§1.1.11 pp.26-27) — the second of which matters more for a grapheme table than anything in qāf. Those are quoted from the thesis; the sections stating the qāf, jīm and kāf reflexes proper were missing from the copy obtained, so no reflex is written here. Writing this spec is a follow-up with the full text, not a guess from what was legible.
